newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Hesse metal firms see wage deal possible.
newsitem.headline: German Hesse metal firms see wage deal possible.

text.p: Metal and engineering employers in the central German state of Hesse said before wage talks due on Wednesday they could accept an agreement similar to the break-through deal signed in Lower Saxony last week.
"We could live with the material aspects of this deal," Dieter Weidemann, chairman of the Hesse metal employers association told journalists at a briefing late on Tuesday night.

Weidemann was referring to the 1997 average labour cost increase of less than one percent estimated to arise from the Lower Saxony package, which failed to implement a new law cutting sick payments by 20 percent.

He said negotiators in Hesse, where many of the near 190,000 metal and engineering workers are employed in small- and medium-sized companies would, however, be seeking a wage package that would leave such employers scope for "internal company solutions."
But he admitted that the scope for negotiation was "very narrow."
Wage talks between the Hesse employers and regional negotiators for the IG Metall trade union start in the town of Mainz on Wednesday.
